get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /ORIGEN_DE_PEDIDO_BET/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Origen de Pedido Beta instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

PARA_PER_SOLO_CON_PADRON.description:
Para las percepciones provinciales (típicamente IIBB), si se aplica este check, sólo se calcularán percepciones si el contribuyente está en el padrón y no aplicará nunca la alícuota máxima.
Si no se aplica el check, y se completa provincia, se calculará la percepción del padrón o la alícuota máxima.

PARA_ASIENTO_ANULACION_MI.title: Asiento Anulación misma Fecha

PARA_UNIFICAR_MOVS_PAT.title: Agrupar cuentas patrimoniales (CC)
PARA_UNIFICAR_MOVS_PAT.description: Si se marca, los movimientos de cuentas patrimoniales (activos, pasivos y patrimonio neto) se agruparán en el asiento contable por cuenta contable, dejando en blanco el centro de costo.

attsFkTexts.description: Descriptive text of every foreign key / user / profile / fixed-value attribute that has a value, keyed by physical name (included when includeFkTexts=true). Example: `"TIDD_ID_TIDD": "CUIT"`. Attributes without a value are omitted, not returned as empty.

schema.description:
A Parámetro instance.

Only Parámetro's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /PARAMETRO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /PARAMETRO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Fast search endpoint. Returns a capped, non-paginated set of Parámetro records; prefer /query for controlled, production-grade listings.
get.description:
Performs a lightweight search over Parámetro instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Parámetro's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /PARAMETRO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /PARAMETRO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

200.description: Matching instances, as a flat array (not wrapped in an object). Child entities are not included.

items.description:
A Parámetro instance.

Only Parámetro's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /PARAMETRO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /PARAMETRO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /PARAMETRO/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - entity name or smartieId empty

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Parámetro instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Empresa's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /EMPRESA/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /EMPRESA/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.description:

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /ZONA/query`.

Performs a lightweight search over Feriado instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Feriado's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /FERIADO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /FERIADO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

200.description: Matching instances, as a flat array (not wrapped in an object). Child entities are not included.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /FERIADO/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)

Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /ORIGENCONTACTO/query`.

Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /CONCEPTO_DE_COMPRAS/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /CONDICION_IVA/query`.

Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /IMPUESTO/query`.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /TIPODEFACTURA/query`.

Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /MONEDA/query`.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /TARJETA/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Concepto de pago electrónico instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /PUESTO_POS/query`.

parameters.name: page

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Puesto POS instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Estado Civil instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /RESULTADO/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Resultado instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /SECTOR/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /GRUPO_MATERIAL/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Grupo de Artículo instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Fast search endpoint. Returns a capped, non-paginated set of Infraestructura records; prefer /query for controlled, production-grade listings.
get.description:
Performs a lightweight search over Infraestructura instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Infraestructura's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /INFRAESTRUCTURA/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /INFRAESTRUCTURA/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

200.description: Matching instances, as a flat array (not wrapped in an object). Child entities are not included.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /INFRAESTRUCTURA/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - entity name or smartieId empty

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Infraestructura instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /TALLE/query`.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /TIPO_UNIDAD/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Tipo de unidad instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /CAI/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on CAI instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /CONDICION_VENTA/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

attsFkTexts.description: Descriptive text of every foreign key / user / profile / fixed-value attribute that has a value, keyed by physical name (included when includeFkTexts=true). Example: `"TIDD_ID_TIDD": "CUIT"`. Attributes without a value are omitted, not returned as empty.

schema.description:
A Origen de Pedido instance.

Only Origen de Pedido's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_Y/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_Y/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Fast search endpoint. Returns a capped, non-paginated set of Origen de Pedido records; prefer /query for controlled, production-grade listings.
get.description:
Performs a lightweight search over Origen de Pedido instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Origen de Pedido's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_Y/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_Y/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

200.description: Matching instances, as a flat array (not wrapped in an object). Child entities are not included.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_Y/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - entity name or smartieId empty

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Origen de Pedido instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /MODIFICACION_DATOS_P/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /TIPO_DE_VENDEDOR/query`.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

get.description:
Performs a lightweight search over Producto Servicio instances. Every query parameter below that matches an attribute's physical name is applied as an equality filter; omit them all to list the first records. The result set is capped and not paginated, so this endpoint is meant for quick lookups. For production listings that require configurable pagination, explicit column selection, or advanced filters, prefer /query.

Only Producto Servicio's own attributes are returned here: a foreign key travels as its id (e.g. `XXXX_ID_XXXX`), not as the referenced instance's description. Columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`) do exist, but they are list columns: request them explicitly through `POST /PRODUCTO_SERVICIO/query` (the `field` enum there lists every available column, related ones included) or add them to a smartie. For a single instance, `GET /PRODUCTO_SERVICIO/{id}?includeFkTexts=true` returns `attsFkTexts` with the descriptive text behind each foreign key.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /PRODUCTO_SERVICIO/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Producto Servicio instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Available columns from `columns` (entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes), plus the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE) which - unlike Usuario ids - are filter-only: filtering by the related id doesn't need the related row's data, only the row's id, so it's supported here even though selecting/sorting by it isn't.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of records matching the query (ignoring pagination)

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`
